Built by cave divers, the system automates the collection of underwater survey data in real time rather than relying solely on manual tape-and-slate measurements.
How the Hardware Works
During an exploration dive, a dual-core processor combines sensor readings 100 times per second to plot the diver's exact path through submerged passages. The unit relies on four core components:
Depth sensor. A high-precision pressure transducer captures accurate vertical depth profiling throughout the dive.
Distance measurement. A magnetic encoder coupled to a wheel tracks how much guideline is deployed .
Compass and IMU. A 9-axis inertial measurement unit records heading, pitch, and roll to determine passage direction and attitude.
Data logger. Internal storage records all raw sensor inputs for detailed post-dive processing and renders a live stick map during the dive.

After a dive, the hardware connects to a computer to process the logged data into standard cartographic outputs.
2D and 3D models. The software generates 2D passage profiles (plan and cross-section views) alongside 3D point cloud visualizations.
Browser-based survey tools. Through the Camazotz Diving Tools Suite , divers can view 3D cave surveys offline directly in a web browser using WebAssembly without creating accounts or uploading data to external servers.
Standard file exports. Processed survey data exports directly into established cave cartography programs like Compass and Walls .
